name: King's Indian chain arrangement (White c4-d5-e4 against Black d6-e5)

plans.label: Strike the base with c4-c5
plans.description: White's break belongs on the queenside because that is where Black's chain can be reached: a pawn arriving on c5 attacks d6, the pawn that holds Black's e5 up. Bring b4, a rook to c1 and the minor pieces first — the pawn is the last move of the plan, not the first.

success.note: A White pawn stands on c5 attacking d6 while both chain heads are still up. Whether the break was properly prepared is not a census fact.

plans.label: Cash the break into the c-file
plans.description: The payoff for the break is the file, not the pawn. However the trade resolves, White wants to come out of it with no pawn of his own on the c-file and the heavy pieces pointing at c7, the square behind Black's base.

success.note: No White pawn stands on the c-file while the d5 and e4 pawns are both still up. Which rook gets there first, and whether it achieves anything, is not a census fact.

plans.label: Blunt the f-pawn before racing
plans.description: The other half of the position is not losing the other wing: a pawn to f3 behind e4, the king's knight rerouted to d3 or d2 rather than left on f3, and a rook stepping to f2 or e1 so that the kingside can be held with fewer pieces than the attack needs.

success.note: The arrangement the plan names, square by square: a pawn on f3, a knight on d3 or d2, and a rook on f2 or e1. The plan states its own squares, so no restatement was needed. Whether the kingside then held is not measured.

plans.label: Strike the base with ...f5
plans.description: Black's break is White's in mirror: a pawn arriving on f5 attacks e4, the pawn that holds White's d5 up. It opens lines beside Black's own king, which is why the knights reroute to e7 and d7 or e8 and the king's rook is ready before the pawn goes.

success.note: A Black pawn stands on f5 attacking e4 while both chain heads are still up. This is the position both shipped King's Indian pack spines end on. CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (D379): a third King's Indian pack has shipped since. The p20-f5 statement still holds for anti-kid-classical-white and kid-classical-black, and this signature also fires at f5-storm, bd2-step, nf6-return and f3-blunt of kid-mar-del-plata-white - 6 firings across three packs, not 2 across two.

plans.label: Lock it with ...f4 and bring the g-pawn
plans.description: Pushing past instead of trading shuts the centre for good. With nothing to be done in the middle the attack becomes pawns — the g-pawn to g5 and g4, the rook behind it — and the position turns into two attacks on opposite wings with no way to interfere with each other.

success.note: Black's f-pawn stands on f4 with White's e4 pawn behind it and the centre still locked. Whether the storm arrives first is exactly what a census cannot say.

plans.label: Put the restraining pieces on the queenside
plans.description: A pawn to a5 against b4, and a pawn to c6 or a knight parked on c5 or b6: each makes the c5 break more expensive. What they cost the kingside attack in tempo is the trade-off, and this entry cannot price it.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Slow the queenside break', whose success was whether the queenside held. It is now the arrangement the plan lists: the a5 pawn plus at least one of the c6 pawn or a knight on c5 or b6. The vocabulary cannot count how many of the three are present, so one of the three is required beside a5. What the restraint cost the kingside attack is still unpriced. Original success note: 'Whether the queenside held is a judgment over many moves, not a property of one position.'

watch: The two breaks are exact mirrors and both are plain pawn geometry: a White pawn on c5 attacks d6, a Black pawn on f5 attacks e4. Each strikes the pawn holding the other side's chain up.
Which break lands first, and what each side spent preparing it.
The attacker and defender count on d6 and on e4 as the preparation arrives.

The dark-squared bishop on g7 belongs to the fianchetto-g7 entry, not to this one. Its diagonal is not empty here: at the shipped King's Indian tabiya three pieces stand between g7 and a1, the nearest of them Black's own e5 pawn. CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (D379): that count is wrong at the tabiya. Four pieces stand between g7 and a1 there - the f6 knight, White's d4 pawn, the c3 knight and the b2 pawn - and the nearest is Black's own knight on f6, not the e5 pawn. Three, with e5 nearest, is what the diagonal reads from p18-nd7 onward, after the knight has left f6 and White has pushed d4-d5. The point the item is making survives the count: the diagonal is never empty anywhere in this structure.
Whether the centre stays shut. The moment either the White d5-e4 pair or the Black d6-e5 pair resolves, this entry stops firing and a different structure is on the board.
typicalMistakes: Attacking where the opponent's chain points instead of at the pawn holding it up.
Pushing the break before the pieces that have to follow it are placed — the pawn arrives alone and is simply taken.

Reusing the French and Caro chain's plans here. The arrangement is reversed, so plan ownership is reversed with it: closed-centre-chain's trigger does not fire on any position in this structure, and its colour-owned plans do not translate.
Trading on f5 or e4 out of discomfort rather than by plan: the trade ends the structure this entry describes and hands the position to whichever side prepared for the open one.
As Black, spending so much on the queenside that the kingside attack never starts — or so little that it never gets to.

sources: COMMISSIONED by the wave-4a opening batch: content/drafts/kid-classical-black.json records in graduationBlockers that no shape entry names the King's Indian pawn-chain arrangement and that its chain teaching is therefore inlined and non-reusable, and content/drafts/anti-kid-classical-white.json records the same gap from the White side. This entry is also the reversed sibling that content/shapes/closed-centre-chain.json's own provenance asked for when it narrowed itself to the French and Caro squares.

MECHANICALLY DERIVED (this session) with the repo's own evaluator — packages/runtime/src/structure.ts matchesStructuralExpression, bundled through the repo's esbuild and driven over positions walked with the repo's chessops dependency. Firing census over all 487 spine positions of the 37 shipped packs in content/drafts: this trigger fires on exactly 14 nodes, the seven from p15-d5 onward in each of the two King's Indian packs (including the b4 Bayonet and the modern knight-to-e8 branch tips), and nowhere else in the corpus. It is false at the standard initial position. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-16 (D379) with `make expression-census` plus a spine walk over the current corpus - 827 authored spine positions across 56 packs under content/drafts and content/packs - and it is the PROPOSITION that changed, not only the numerals: this trigger fires on 24 nodes across THREE packs, so 'and nowhere else in the corpus' is false and is withdrawn. The reading is anti-kid-classical-white 7 (p15-d5 p16-ne7 p17-ne1 p18-nd7 p19-f3 p20-f5 b4-bayonet) and kid-classical-black 7 (p15-d5 p16-ne7 p17-ne1 p18-nd7 p19-f3 p20-f5 ne8-modern) - both exactly as the sentence above describes them, unmoved - plus kid-mar-del-plata-white 10 (start ne1-reroute nd7-clear nd3-post f5-storm bd2-step nf6-return f3-blunt f4-lock be3-alternative), a pack that did not exist when this line was written and whose own start position already stands inside the structure. So 487 -> 827 and 14 -> 24, and the two named packs' own counts did not move: the whole increase is the third pack. Still false at the standard initial position, re-checked.

MECHANICALLY DERIVED (this session), the mirroring claim: closed-centre-chain's trigger was evaluated against every position where this entry fires and matches none of them, and this trigger was evaluated against a constructed French Advance chain and does not match it. The two entries are disjoint on the shipped corpus, which is what the wave-4a blockers asserted and nothing had checked.

MECHANICALLY DERIVED (this session), the geometry the prose states as fact: a White pawn on c5 attacks b6 and d6; a Black pawn on f5 attacks e4 and g4; a White pawn on e4 attacks d5 and f5; a Black pawn on d6 attacks c5 and e5 — so each break lands on the square supporting the opposing chain head, in both directions. At the shipped tabiya the g7 bishop's line to a1 carries exactly three blockers. CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (D379): the pawn-attack half of this line re-derives exactly as stated - each of the four attack pairs was re-counted with the repo's own direct_attack_count on a bare board and reads 1 on both named squares and 0 on the squares beside them - but the blocker count is wrong at the position it names. At the shipped King's Indian tabiya, meaning the start position of anti-kid-classical-white and of kid-classical-black, the g7-a1 diagonal carries FOUR blockers: the f6 knight, White's d4 pawn, the c3 knight and the b2 pawn. Exactly three is the reading only from p18-nd7 onward, once the knight has left f6 and White's d-pawn has gone to d5. Across all 24 positions where this entry now fires the count is 3 or 4 and never fewer.

MECHANICALLY DERIVED (this session), plan success signatures: each non-null signature was evaluated on a legally reached position that satisfies it and on a reference position that does not. The c5 strike fires after the break is played; the c-file signature after the trade resolves; the ...f5 signature fires at p20-f5, the last spine node of both King's Indian packs, so those packs now end inside a named plan's success condition rather than beside one; the ...f4 signature after the pawn pushes past. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-16 (D379) over 827 positions: the p20-f5 statement still holds in both packs, and the same signature now also fires at f5-storm, bd2-step, nf6-return and f3-blunt of kid-mar-del-plata-white, 6 firings in all across three packs. The other four signatures are corpus-visible too and were counted in the same run: white-strike-the-base-with-c5 2 (kid-mar-del-plata-white c5-break, g5-storm), white-cash-the-break-into-the-c-file 0, white-blunt-the-f-pawn 0, black-lock-with-f4-and-storm 3 (kid-mar-del-plata-white f4-lock, c5-break, g5-storm), black-slow-the-queenside 1 - and that one is in carlsbad-minority-attack (a5-prophylaxis), outside this structure, which is what an arrangement signature with no chain conjunct will do.

TRIGGER SCOPE, stated rather than implied. The c4 pawn is required, following the commissioning blockers' own wording. Verified consequence: the Czech Benoni arrangement fires (checked on a constructed position), because it is the same five-pawn skeleton with the same plan ownership. Chains of the same shape reached without a pawn on c4 — King's Indian Attack setups, closed Spanish structures — do NOT fire, and are not claimed. Two known limits: the trigger says nothing about where either king castled, and it cannot distinguish a chain that is about to resolve from one that is locked, because no vocabulary here counts what may capture next.

NOT DUPLICATED: the g7 bishop's plans, including the long-diagonal signature, are owned by content/shapes/fianchetto-g7.json, which fires on every position of both King's Indian packs. This entry deliberately carries no bishop plan; the watch list points at the other entry instead. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-16 (D379): 'both King's Indian packs' is now three, and the coverage claim needs the qualifier it did not need when there were two. fianchetto-g7's trigger still fires on every position of anti-kid-classical-white (14 of 14) and of kid-classical-black (13 of 13), and on 11 of the 12 positions of kid-mar-del-plata-white. The ownership statement the sentence exists to support is unaffected: this entry still carries no bishop plan.

UNGROUNDED: every strategic claim here — all six plan descriptions, the non-derived watch items and typical mistakes, the whole attack-the-base doctrine the plan structure assumes, and every judgment about what a plan is worth — is agent-authored prose with no citation, no engine evaluation, no corpus frequency and no human review. What is machine-derived is labelled above; everything else is assertion.
